COMPLETE EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Primary method:  Difference-in-Differences (DID) with an event-study
parameterisation.

• Why DID?  We need a counterfactual path for the abnormal returns of firms that
make the “Best Companies” list.  DID compares the post-announcement excess
returns of listed firms (treated) with those of very similar, non-listed firms
(control), netting out time-varying macro factors common to all stocks.  

• Why embed an event study?  We want to trace the dynamic pattern of abnormal
returns (t = -12 … +60 months) to see whether any alpha is earned only
immediately after publication or persists for several years.  Estimating
lead/lag coefficients also delivers a visual pre-trend test of the DID
parallel-trends assumption.

Technically, we will estimate:

α_it = Σ_{k≠-1} β_k · 1[τ_i = k] + γ_i + δ_t + X_itΛ + ε_it,

where α_it is the monthly four-factor abnormal return of firm i in month t,
τ_i = (t – event_date_i) is the month-relative-to-event, γ_i are firm fixed
effects, and δ_t are calendar-month fixed effects.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Treatment variable
  Treat_it = 1 for firm i in all months t ≥ January of the calendar year in
  which it first appears in Fortune’s list; 0 otherwise.

Event date / treatment timing
  January of the list year (the month the magazine is released to investors).

Control group
  • Preferred:  Nearest-neighbour matched firms (1–3 matches) that
    – operate in the same 2-digit SIC industry,
    – are in the same NYSE size decile in December of t-1,
    – are in the same book-to-market tercile, and
    – have similar 12-month momentum (±5 p.p.).  
  • Alternative:  All firms that never appear on any list (“never-treated”),
    with weights from inverse propensity scores to re-balance observables.

Rationale:  The matched firms provide a plausible return benchmark while
avoiding look-ahead bias.

Running variable and cutoff
  Not applicable (RDD not used).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A1. Parallel trends.  In the absence of treatment, list firms and matched
controls would have followed the same path of abnormal returns.

  Plausibility:  Matching on industry, size, B/M, and momentum plus inclusion
  of firm and month FE makes this credible.  Will be empirically assessed with
  pre-event leads (-12 … ‑2).

A2. No differential shocks at the event date other than the public ­list
announcement.

  Plausibility: The list is released on a fixed annual schedule; no concurrent
  earnings announcements occur systemically in early January.  We will test for
  clustering of confounding events.

A3. SUTVA / no spill-overs.  Inclusion of one firm does not directly change the
returns of its control firms.

  Plausibility:  Stock-level spill-overs are unlikely except for closest
  competitors; we mitigate by excluding same corporate parents and conducting
  robustness checks that drop closest rivals.

A4. No anticipatory trading (or, if anticipation exists, it is visible as
pre-trend and can be accounted for).

  Plausibility:  The list is based on confidential employee surveys and is hard
  to predict.  We will look for excess returns in the six months prior.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & MITIGATION
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
T1. Endogenous selection / omitted intangibles
   – Firms may be selected precisely because they are already improving in ways
     that also raise returns (culture, innovation wave, etc.).
   Mitigation:  (i) Tight matching on observable fundamentals and momentum;
               (ii) Include firm FE, which absorb any time-invariant driver;
               (iii) Instrumental-variable placebo: use future winners as a
               falsification control (they should not earn alpha pre-listing).

T2. Survival and look-ahead bias in CRSP/Compustat.
   Mitigation:  (i) Use CRSP with share-code & exch-code filters and
               delisting-return adjustments; (ii) Require that controls are
               alive and liquid at the event date, not at the analysis date.

T3. Contamination by January seasonality.
   Mitigation:  Calendar-month fixed effects soak up the turn-of-year effect;
               re-estimate on return residuals that have January-lag demeaned
               factors; run placebo “pseudo events” in April.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5. R CODE OUTLINE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```r
# 0. Packages -----------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)
library(fixest)      # fast high-dim FE estimation
library(MatchIt)     # nearest neighbour matching
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load data ----------------------------------------------------------
list   <- fread("fortune_best_companies_1984_2009.csv")   # columns: cik, year
ret    <- fread("crsp_monthly_returns.csv")               # permno, date, ret
comp   <- fread("compustat_annual.csv")                   # cik, year, at, bkvlps
ff4    <- fread("ff_carhart_factors_monthly.csv")         # date, mkt, smb, hml, mom, rf

# 2. Variable construction ---------------------------------------------
# a) Map CIK to PERMNO (assume mapping file)
link   <- fread("cik_permno_link.csv")
list   <- merge(list, link, by = "cik", allow.cartesian = TRUE)

# b) Event date: first appearance
list   <- list[order(year), .(first_year = min(year)), by = permno]

# c) Merge returns & factors
ret    <- merge(ret, ff4, by = "date")
ret[, excess := ret - rf]

# d) Four-factor abnormal return (alpha) via rolling regression 36m window
#    For simplicity: subtract factor returns weighted by full-sample betas
betas <- ret[ , {
            fit <- lm(excess ~ mkt + smb + hml + mom)
            coef(fit)[-1]                        # skip intercept
        }, by = permno]

ret    <- merge(ret, betas, by = "permno")
ret[, ff_alpha := excess - (mkt*`mkt` + smb*`smb` + hml*`hml` + mom*`mom`)]

# e) Treat indicator
ret <- merge(ret, list,
             by = "permno", all.x = TRUE)
ret[, treat := 0L]
ret[!is.na(first_year) & year(date) >= first_year, treat := 1L]

# f) Event-time
ret[, event_time := 999L]
ret[!is.na(first_year),
    event_time := 12*(year(date) - first_year) + (month(date) - 1)]

# g) Keep balanced sample window
ret <- ret[event_time >= -12*3 & event_time <= 12*5]  # -3y … +5y

# 3. Matching (1-to-1 nearest neighbour) -------------------------------
prevars <- c("size_decile", "bm_terc", "mom12", "sic2")
# assume these vars already merged in 'ret' at t = -1 month

match_data <- unique(ret[month(date)==12 & event_time==-1,
                         c("permno","treat", prevars), with=FALSE])

m.out <- matchit(treat ~ size_decile + bm_terc + mom12 + sic2,
                 data = match_data, method = "nearest", ratio = 1)
matched <- data.table(match.data(m.out))[, .(permno)]

ret <- ret[permno %in% matched$permno]

# 4. Event-study DID regression ----------------------------------------
ret[, event_factor := factor(event_time)]
est <- feols(ff_alpha ~ i(event_time, treat, ref = -1) | permno + date,
             data = ret, cluster = ~permno)

# 5. Plot coefficients --------------------------------------------------
iplot(est) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype="dashed") +
  ylab("Monthly 4-factor alpha (bp)") + xlab("Months relative to listing")

# 6. Robustness: exclude January returns -------------------------------
robust <- feols(ff_alpha ~ i(event_time, treat, ref = -1) | permno + date,
                data = ret[month(date)!=1], cluster = ~permno)
summary(robust)
```

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6. EXPECTED RESULTS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Theory predicts that if markets under-price intangibles:

• Direction: β_{0,+1,+2,…} > 0  →  positive abnormal returns after the list is
  published.

• Magnitude: The literature on intangibles and existing back-of-the-envelope
  calculations suggest ≈ 3–4 percent annualised four-factor alpha for list
  firms (≈ 25–35 basis points per month) over a 3- to 5-year horizon, with
  roughly half of the total abnormal return realised in the first year.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (Difference-in-Differences)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
C1: Pre-trend (visual & statistical)                           1  
C2: No simultaneous confounding shocks                        0.5  
C3: SUTVA / no spill-overs                                     1  
C4: Stable composition & no differential attrition            1  
C5: No anticipation / timing exogeneity                       0.5  

Overall: 4 / 5 – credible but not bullet-proof.
